title: Remap text works, same keys will not launch program, inconsistent

status.label: Retest run-program action on a current build
status.detail: The issue reports PowerToys 0.97.2 on Windows 11; the same chord can emit remapped text but reportedly does not launch Notepad or Obsidian. There is no current-build test or diagnostic capture.

judgment.rationale: The report gives a useful contrast: Ctrl+Shift+P can emit text, but a run-program mapping for Notepad does not launch, and Obsidian behavior was inconsistent. The environment is Windows 11 and PowerToys 0.97.2, with no comments or current-build retest. Because the launch path also depends on the selected run-program fields and If running action, request a targeted current-build retest and a fresh diagnostic only if it still fails; do not infer a root cause from the text mapping succeeding.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.97.2 on Windows 11 and says a Ctrl+Shift+P text remap works while a run-program mapping does not.
The reporter says Notepad can be launched with the Windows Run command and that the PowerToys run-program action did not launch it.
The report also describes inconsistent behavior for Obsidian and a one-time application breakpoint error.
The issue has no comments or assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to retest the Notepad run-program mapping on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer, confirm the mapping fields and If running choice, and provide /bugreport only if it still fails.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report predates current builds and leaves the exact run-program path, arguments, and If running action unresolved. A current, controlled retest is needed before a code fix can be grounded.

issue_context.summary: A Ctrl+Shift+P text mapping works, but the same shortcut reportedly fails to launch Notepad or sometimes Obsidian on PowerToys 0.97.2.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.97.2, Windows 11, and says the text action fires for Ctrl+Shift+P.
The reporter says a run-program mapping for Notepad did not launch, although Windows Run could launch Notepad.
The report describes inconsistent Obsidian behavior and one application breakpoint error.
There are no issue comments, assignees, or current-build diagnostics.
inferences: The reported difference may be in run-program configuration or process handling rather than shortcut detection, but the exact mapping fields and current behavior are unknown.
issue_context.analysis: The same chord reaching the text action narrows the symptom to the run-program path, but it does not establish that the current build has the same failure. Retest with a simple executable and inspect the exact path/arguments and If running setting; request diagnostics only if that controlled case still fails.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report and noted its Windows 11, PowerToys 0.97.2, text-versus-run-program comparison, and no-comment state.
No exact path, arguments, current If running selection, or current-build result is stated in the body.

comment.body:
Thanks for the contrast between the working text action and the failing run-program action. The report lists PowerToys 0.97.2, so the current behavior is not yet established. Could you please:
1. Retest the same Ctrl+Shift+P mapping on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer with Notepad as the run-program target, and report whether it launches.
2. If it still fails, share the target path, arguments, start-in directory, and If running selection (redacting unrelated personal path components).
3. Comment `/bugreport` immediately after the current-build failure.
This will separate a run-program configuration issue from a failure in the current launch path.
